newsitem.title: GREECE: Piraeus Bank teams up with Sigma Securities.
newsitem.headline: Piraeus Bank teams up with Sigma Securities.

text.p: Piraeus Bank has acquired a 30 percent stake in Athens stock exchange member Sigma Securities following the approval by the Bank of Greece and the capital market commission.
Under the deal, Piraeus Bank retains an option to acquire an additional 21 percent in the first half of 1998 and raise its stake to 51 percent.

Sigma Securities managing director John Marcopoulos will retain his post for at least six years. He steered Sigma to the top tier among the exchange's 63 brokers since its launch in May 1990 as the first private brokerage.
Joining forces in a strategic deal will benefit both firms. Piraeus Bank emerges with a stake in one of the leading and most profitable Greek brokers, expanding its range of services.

For Sigma Securities, teaming up with fast-growing Piraeus Bank will mean access to its branch network as well as operational and financial backing, it said in a statement. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
